assessment: SOURCE 1–2 show the same elongated building from its ramped short end and adjoining long side: a recessed lower frame, projecting two-level glazed enclosure, zigzag exterior ramps and a concave timber roof with unequal edge heights. SOURCE 3 shows the glazed entrance and an open gallery beneath grating supported by transverse beams. SOURCE 4 shows the curved timber ceiling, guarded circular floor openings, spiral stair and lower concrete-framed workspace. SOURCE 5–8 establish the perimeter buffer, retained frame, added upper hall and differing floor/void relationships through sections, exploded diagrams and plans; these are not exterior cutaway views. CURRENT captures the broad arrangement, but reverses defining end relationships, substitutes solid gallery construction and leaves a visible floor opening unguarded. No confirmed dimensions are supplied. The blank lower-interior image and repeated uncut views cannot verify internal floor connections or concealed joints.

issues.problem: SOURCE 1’s end views show the roof’s right edge higher than its left and the upper ramp descending toward the right. CURRENT 15 shows the opposite roof-edge hierarchy and upper-ramp direction. Ramp/rail extensions also project beyond the enclosure without clearly resolved landing connections.
issues.action: Locally correct the roof edge heights and ramp handedness against the same source end landmarks. Trim extensions and connect each flight to its corresponding landing with continuous walking surfaces and guards; preserve the established concave roof concept.

issues.problem: SOURCE 3 shows a light, permeable grating deck overhead with distinct transverse support beams. CURRENT 19 presents a continuous solid soffit with no comparable exposed beam rhythm. CURRENT 16–18 also read as heavy dark railing grids and opaque horizontal bands, obscuring the source’s light glazed buffer and open gallery.
issues.action: Patch the gallery deck to show the source-backed grating and exposed support bays. Reduce excessive rail/frame bulk and apply the observed pale frame finish and transparent glazing, retaining actual floor-edge structure.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 shows mesh guards surrounding the visible circular floor openings. CURRENT 20 has a large foreground opening with no perimeter guard, while the farther stair opening has a coarse bar enclosure. The foreground opening’s exact placement cannot be confirmed from this camera.
issues.action: Add a continuous mesh guard around the exposed foreground opening and refine the stair-opening guard to the source’s light assembly. Check opening locations against SOURCE 7 before changing their positions; verify that stair flights terminate at real floor openings.

keep: The roof’s continuous concave curvature.
The upper hall’s visible timber ceiling material zone.
The repeated pale columns along the lower glazed frontage.

Source 3 shows the recessed entrance and open grated gallery; source 4 shows the timber ceiling, circular floor openings, spiral stair and double-height lower workspace. issues.action: Locally revise the gallery deck, soffit and edge assembly to expose the observed beam-and-grating construction. Check inclined support endpoints against actual structural members rather than accepting apparent screen-space contact.

assessment: SOURCE exterior perspectives show an elongated glazed building, a recessed lower frame, projecting circulation decks, end ramps, and a raised roof with an asymmetric sagging profile. The aerial panel establishes its length; sections and plans establish a double-height lower interior, partial intermediate floor, room partitions and circular openings. Interior panels show pale floors, concrete framing, a timber ceiling and mesh guards around openings. These recurring landmarks identify the same building across the collages; no numerical dimensions are confirmed. CURRENT retains the recognizable roof profile and circulation arrangement, but continuous floor plates, exaggerated ramp-end projections and incomplete opening guards materially change the observed architecture. Screenshots cannot establish whether all deck, ramp and brace connections are physically joined; hidden connections remain unverified.

issues.problem: CURRENT has continuous intermediate slabs across the lower interior, whereas SOURCE sections 5 and 8 show a substantial double-height space beside a partial intermediate floor. CURRENT also reads as largely undivided framing where SOURCE plans and interior views show enclosed room zones.
issues.action: Locally trim the intermediate slab to the source-backed void boundary and add the visible room partitions and glazed boundaries using plans 5 and 7. Preserve correctly positioned columns rather than replacing the frame.

issues.problem: CURRENT ramp landings project conspicuously beyond both sides of the end enclosure. In SOURCE 1 and 2, these returns sit much closer to the surrounding deck edges, producing a tighter end silhouette.
issues.action: Shorten and reposition the projecting landing returns to match the source end views. Maintain continuous ramp-to-landing and landing-to-deck geometry, checking each junction rather than relying on overlapping edges.

issues.problem: CURRENT view 18 shows two circular floor openings without perimeter guards. SOURCE interior panel 4 shows raised cylindrical mesh guards around the corresponding openings; these are substantial spatial elements, not decorative trim.
issues.action: Add continuous circular mesh guards at the exposed openings, seated on their slab rims, matching the source proportions and retaining the existing stair enclosure where appropriate.

assessment: SOURCE panels show one elongated building: a recessed concrete frame, a timber upper hall beneath a sagging roof, a projecting glazed perimeter, and stacked ramps at one short end. CURRENT captures the principal exterior arrangement, but the interior remains substantially more open, receiving landings meet uninterrupted glazing, and several upper-floor holes lack guards. Geographic orientation and exact dimensions are not established by the source images; the uncut CURRENT views cannot verify every internal connection.

issues.problem: SOURCE plans and sections show enclosed lower-storey rooms and an asymmetric double-height interior. CURRENT views 15–17 and 23–25 expose largely uninterrupted floor plates and bare columns, omitting major internal spatial boundaries.
issues.action: Locally add the source-visible room enclosures and correct the corresponding floor opening for the double-height space. Retain correctly positioned structural members; use the source plans and sections together to locate these patches.

issues.problem: CURRENT views 23–26 show continuous glass panels and framing across the apparent receiving passages. issues.action: At each receiving passage, provide an actual opening or operable door through the glazing, aligned with the landing and interior access. Resolve any brace crossing that passage locally, preserving adjacent glazing.

issues.problem: SOURCE interior panel 4 shows circular floor openings enclosed by raised mesh guards. CURRENT view 18 shows the foreground and middle circular holes with exposed, unguarded edges; only the distant stair opening has a guard.
issues.action: Add circular mesh guards around the exposed openings, joined to the floor perimeter, matching the source’s slender posts and raised top rail.

assessment: SOURCE panels show one elongated building: a concrete lower frame, stepped intermediate floors with a double-height region, a timber upper hall beneath a sagging roof, an outer glazed buffer, projecting circulation decks and three sloping ramp runs at one short end. Recurring ramps, roof supports and circular stair openings connect the exterior, interior, section and plan views. CURRENT captures these broad exterior elements, but close views reveal unresolved diagonal-support connections and substantially heavier circulation assemblies. The uncut section views and roof-covered plan cannot verify the source’s internal floor voids or room arrangement. No numerical dimensions are confirmed by the supplied evidence.

issues.problem: Repeated diagonal rods visibly terminate in circulation space below the soffit, with exposed ends above the deck. SOURCE sections and model photographs show diagonals continuing between structural attachment points; these are not intended shadow gaps.
issues.action: Locally extend, trim or reposition each affected diagonal to meet its actual upper and lower supporting members. Resolve the deck/soffit penetrations and retain a clear walking route.

issues.problem: Heavy stacked horizontal rails and opaque grey circulation decks dominate CURRENT. SOURCE 1–3 show slender pale frames, fine mesh guards and visibly permeable grating with exposed supporting beams. The current assembly obscures the glazing and changes the building’s defining lightness.
issues.action: Patch the ramp and balcony guards to fine mesh within slender frames, and revise the shown deck surfaces and undersides to the source-backed grating-and-beam assembly. Preserve the matching ramp directions.

issues.problem: A circular floor opening in the foreground has no raised guard, while SOURCE 4 upper shows prominent cylindrical mesh guards around the visible circular openings. The existing guarded stair opening does not resolve this separate exposed opening.
issues.action: Add the missing cylindrical mesh guard to the corresponding opening, matching its rim and source-visible height; verify the other visible circular openings individually.

keep: Three descending ramp runs across the short end.
Concave transverse roof profile with unequal edge heights.
Slender timber uprights visible around the upper hall.

assessment: SOURCE 1–2 establish the ramp end and adjoining long facade: a recessed building frame, three descending ramp flights, projecting galleries, a transparent upper enclosure and a raised concave timber roof. SOURCE 3 shows the glazed entrance and gallery underside; SOURCE 4 shows the curved timber ceiling, pale floor, curtain divisions and guarded circular openings. SOURCE 5 and 8 show stepped interior floor levels and substantial voids; SOURCE 6 separates the structural layers; all three SOURCE 7 plans show distinct floor arrangements. CURRENT captures the principal exterior composition, but its enclosure reads substantially heavier and its upper interior remains incomplete. The uncut section views and roof-occluded plan cannot establish whether the concealed floor arrangements match. No numerical dimensions were supplied, and screenshots alone cannot certify concealed joints.

issues.problem: CURRENT 16–17 substitutes prominent stacked rails and heavy framing for the source’s slender white enclosure and fine mesh gallery guards. This obscures the recessed glazing and overwhelms the otherwise comparable massing.
issues.action: Locally reduce the visible frame and rail sections, apply the source’s light finish, and replace coarse horizontal guard infill with fine mesh where shown. Preserve the gallery positions and ramp slopes.

issues.problem: CURRENT 18 shows circular floor openings without surrounding guards, while SOURCE 4 shows continuous cylindrical mesh protection. The existing guarded opening does not resolve the exposed openings elsewhere.
issues.action: Match the source-backed opening locations and fit continuous mesh guards around their exposed perimeters, seated on the floor and connected at their returns.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 shows a pale floor and large curved translucent curtain divisions beneath the timber ceiling. CURRENT 18 instead has an uninterrupted brown floor and lacks those prominent spatial divisions.
issues.action: Change the upper floor to the observed pale finish and add the visible curved curtain tracks and translucent hanging panels. Retain the concave timber ceiling.

keep: Concave roof end profile with its higher right edge in the matched ramp-end view.

Open gallery underside with projecting transverse beams and recessed glazing.
